title: Intermittent service-discovery shadowing after tenant VNI reshuffle
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Several Dedicated customers reported transient failures where DNS responses for short-TTL service discovery records were delivered to the wrong tenant. Symptoms were intermittent 5xxs in control-plane logs and spurious cross-tenant resolution observed from customer app logs during autoscale/reshuffle events.

Repro steps (observed in staging reproduction):
1) Provision two tenants A and B on the same Dedicated GPU pool.
2) Trigger a scale-down that drains a node, forcing VNI reassignment and egress SNAT rebind.
3) Generate high-rate DNS queries (TTL=1–5s) from both tenants during the reshuffle window.
4) Observe DNS replies occasionally arriving at the egress flow associated with the other tenant; conntrack entries show persistent tuple mapping despite VNI change.

Root cause analysis:
- The control plane reassigns overlay VNI identifiers during tenant reshuffle. VNI assignment can reuse recently freed IDs before dataplane egress binding (SNAT metadata) is reconciled.
- Ephemeral conntrack entries persisted in a shared conntrack namespace during fast node detach/attach. When a recycled VNI was assigned to a different tenant, existing conntrack tuples remained bound to the previous egress mapping, allowing replies (especially UDP DNS replies) to be NATed back into the wrong tenant's flow.
- Short DNS TTLs and high query burst rates increased the probability window for a collision.

Mitigation applied (hotfix):
- Deployed edge-proxy response-guard (hotfix) that tags DNS replies with tenant cookie and drops responses whose cookie does not match the current egress binding. This prevents cross-tenant delivery while we fix dataplane reconciliation. Rolled to affected Dedicated clusters at 2026-03-12 03:00 UTC.
- Added temporary aggressive conntrack eviction for UDP flows when VNI rebinds are detected.

Permanent fix plan:
1) Dataplane change: move to deterministic, monotonic VNI assignment per-tenant to avoid immediate reuse of freed VNIs within a safe cooldown window.
2) Isolation hardening: ensure tenant-specific conntrack namespaces (netns) or strict conntrack keying that includes tenant ID to prevent tuple reuse across tenants.
3) Add egress binding reconciliation barrier so that control plane does not mark a VNI free until dataplane confirms conntrack and SNAT state cleared.
4) Improve observability: instrument VNI lifecycle events, conntrack eviction rate, and DNS mismatch alerts.

Rollout strategy:
- Implement dataplane deterministic VNI assignment and netns migration in runtime-1.23 canary pool first.
- Run soak test with synthetic DNS TTL bursts and tenant reshuffle scenarios for 72 hours.
- Gradual rollout to all Dedicated regions; provide targeted patch backport to 1.22 for highest-impact customers.

Customer comms:
- Initial customer-facing note sent 2026-03-12; support ticket batch ID: SUP-6684. We promised a root cause summary and ETA for permanent fix (3 weeks).

References and artifacts:
- Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/ENG-998877+service-discovery-shadowing
- Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/12988
- Dataplane design doc (draft): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3cVni-redwood-vni-design
